notes: Limitations relative to the requested every-swap payment, first: the fee is paid to the recipient inside the swap only when the PoolManager's IMD balance at afterSwap covers it and the IMD token accepts the transfer. Routers settle the swap's input after the hook runs, so every sell pays at once, but a buy pays at once only when the manager already holds at least the fee in IMD from earlier trades; on the launch pool, seeded with RNNN only, the first buys and any buy whose fee exceeds the manager's IMD are deferred. A deferred fee is recorded as an ERC-6909 claim on IMD held by the hook, never lost or reduced; the next swap that finds enough IMD in the manager pays all pending claims to the recipient along with its own fee, and anyone may call the permissionless redeemPendingFees at any time, which pays what the manager's IMD covers. The live IMD token has an admin blocklist: if the recipient is ever blocked, the direct transfer reverts, the hook catches it and defers the fee as a claim, trading continues, and claims pay out once unblocked. Swaps that specify IMD (exact-input buy, exact-output sell) run the pool's swap math twice (a reverting self-call simulation), so they cost roughly a swap's gas again. beforeInitialize does not restrict the initializer or the other currency, so anyone may open another IMD pool on this hook; it is charged the same way to the same recipient. RnnnFeeHook serves the rnnn.bid (RNNN)/IMD launch pool on Robinhood Chain (4663). Constructor arguments, in declaration order: the PoolManager, the IMD token 0x5f7bb59365ce557c26dbcaa4ee9d39a4b95b7127 and the fee recipient 0x45c89d0cf0b8a05218506236fcfcb18da1d3ebe4, all immutable and all given by the launch or the brief. The hook does not take the launch token or an owner: it finds IMD by address in the PoolKey and has no owner, pause, fee setter, token minting authority, upgrade path or other hook fee; no function is restricted to a privileged address, and simulateSwap accepts only the hook itself and always reverts. Fees are always IMD, 1% of the IMD side (floor of amount * 100 / 10000), and are never swapped or sold for ETH or any other token, on the requester's explicit instruction and against the IMD default of settling hook fees in ETH. When IMD is the specified currency, beforeSwap simulates the swap and returns a specified delta of 1% of the IMD the pool will move (1% of the requested amount on a full fill, 1% of the filled amount on a short fill); afterSwap settles that same amount from transient storage. When IMD is the unspecified currency (exact-output buy, exact-input sell), afterSwap returns an unspecified delta of 1% of the pool's IMD delta. A swap that moves no IMD pays nothing. The LP fee is never overridden; the 1% hook fee is additional to the 1.25% LP fee. beforeInitialize accepts only the PoolManager as caller, requires IMD on either side, refuses dynamic-fee pools, and accepts the launch's 12500 LP fee and tick spacing 60. Every enabled callback and unlockCallback accept only the PoolManager. The hook address must carry permission bits 0x20cc. RnnnToken takes no constructor arguments and reports rnnn.bid, RNNN and 18 decimals. Foundry tests cover funded buys and sells in both exact-input and exact-output modes paying exactly 1% of the IMD side to the recipient, deferred fees and redemption on an RNNN-only pool, short fills, the blocked-recipient case, permission flags, callback access and the absence of privileged functions. pool.initialPrice records the required reference value; the deployer derives the opening price from the launch policy.
